clue.text: Answer supporters with 'This compiler's harsh'

parts.note: bras are garments that give support
the setter speaking of themself: 'I have' contracts to I'VE

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that their answers carry a harsh edge, with supporters backing the claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This compiler's' is the setter talking about themself, so 'This compiler has' gives I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rough and grating in manner is harsh, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Put in chapter adopted by technology user

parts.note: to add is to put something in

indicators.note: adopted by means the chapter letter is taken into the technology letters

parts.note: IT stands for information technology

explanation.surface: A tech user has a new chapter put into their manual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'user' looks like a computer user; it means a drug user. 'adopted by' puts C inside IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug user hooked on a substance is an addict-type user in slang.

clue.text: Part in affair is questionably improper

indicators.note: Part in means a section lies within the words affair is questionably

explanation.surface: Playing a role in a love affair is of questionable propriety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part in' signals the answer sits inside 'affair is questionably'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly indecent or racy, bordering on the improper, an adjective borrowed from French.

clue.text: Barber cut back around crown of head

indicators.note: around says the economising word encloses the letter from head

parts.note: to save is to cut back on spending

indicators.note: crown of means the top or first letter of the word head

explanation.surface: A barber trims back hair around the crown of a client's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barber' is a verb here: to barber someone is to trim their beard. 'around' puts SAVE round H.
explanation.definitionFit: To barber is to cut hair or remove a beard with a razor, a verb sense.

clue.text: Protection against a cold reportedly identified

parts.note: V is short for versus, against

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for identified is spoken and we enter its sound

parts.note: seen means spotted or identified

explanation.surface: A news item says protection against a cold has been identified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' gives CINE as the sound of SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A jab giving immunity to disease is protection against it.

clue.text: About to flip in circuit going very fast

indicators.note: in says the flipped letters go inside the word for circuit

parts.note: a ring is a circular track or circuit

indicators.note: to flip means the abbreviation for about is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A driver about to lose control and flip over on a race circuit at high speed.
explanation.walkthrough: CA (circa) is the usual crossword shorthand for about.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing car or heart is one moving at great speed, so the participle means going very fast.

clue.text: Left a party with single daughter

parts.note: a band is a party or group of people
one is a single unit

explanation.surface: A woman left a party with only her one daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserted or forsaken, left behind, is the past participle sense.

clue.text: Grateful Iron Duke with bravest ended losing heart

indicators.note: losing heart means each of the words Iron, Duke, bravest and ended keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A tribute to Wellington, the Iron Duke, as the bravest who ended up dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Duke' looks like Wellington; 'losing heart' strips the middle from each of the four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Owing someone thanks for a favour makes you grateful to them, the figurative sense of owing.

clue.text: Goods host always served up — money welcome

indicators.note: host means the pair of good letters plays host to what follows, enclosing it

parts.note: G is short for good, so goods gives two of them

indicators.note: served up means the word for always is turned upside down in this down clue

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A host serves up goods, always welcoming guests with money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns EER to REE in a down clue; GG 'host' REE plus TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of welcome is a salutation, as when hosts receive guests.

clue.text: Range of opinion on dais occasionally

indicators.note: on says the opinion comes after the letters taken from the platform
occasionally means only some letters of the word dais are used, every other one

parts.note: a stance is a position or opinion held

explanation.surface: A speaker on the platform airs a range of opinion from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes alternate letters of 'dais', D and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is how far something reaches, which is a span or extent of space.

clue.text: Initially walk as ducks do, leaning excessively

definitions.text: Initially walk as ducks do, leaning excessively

indicators.note: Initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A description of how ducks walk, rolling from side to side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes the first letters of 'walk as ducks do leaning excessively', and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk with short swaying steps like a duck, tilting from side to side, is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Rose say, to get examined

indicators.note: say means the colour word is spoken and we enter a word sounding the same

parts.note: rose is a pinkish red colour

explanation.surface: Someone named Rose, say, is to be examined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a name or flower; it is the colour. The past tense of the verb is pronounced like the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Having looked through a text carefully is to have examined it, past tense.

clue.text: Held crop up, it's heard, producing burn

indicators.note: it's heard means the phrase is spoken and we enter what it sounds like

parts.note: held means caught; to crop up is to arise

explanation.surface: A farmer held back a crop that came up, leading to a burn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's heard' says CAUGHT ARISE spoken aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors seal a wound by searing it with heat or chemicals, which is to burn it.

clue.text: Money owed to cover University entrance

indicators.note: to cover means the word for money owed wraps round the university letter

parts.note: money owed is a debt

explanation.surface: A student takes on debt to pay for their university entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' wraps DEBT round U.
explanation.definitionFit: A first appearance on stage or in a team is an entrance, the noun sense.

clue.text: For section of Church sin's not large

indicators.note: not means the letter for large is left out of the word for sin

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or sin; the 's is 'is' linking to what follows

explanation.surface: A churchgoer muses that for church, sin isn't too big a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes L (large) from LAPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rounded end of a church, usually behind the altar, is a section of the building.

clue.text: Most prudish minister accepts one's heartless sins

indicators.note: accepts means the minister takes the following letters inside

parts.note: a priest is a minister of religion
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's links it to the sins

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of the word sins is removed

explanation.surface: A prudish minister accepts the confession of someone's sins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips the middle IN from 'sins'; the 's after 'one' only joins it to the sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Being excessively prim and fussy about propriety, in the superlative degree.

clue.text: Keep manure working round top of earth

indicators.note: round says the manure-plus-working letters go round the letter taken from earth

parts.note: dung is animal manure
on means working, as a machine is on

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of the word earth

explanation.surface: A gardener instructs: keep the manure working into the topsoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a castle's strongest tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle keep and an underground cell are both strongholds; the crossword sense of keep is a castle tower or prison.

clue.text: Batted, never getting upset about rivalry

indicators.note: getting upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
about here means within the area of, so the letters are found inside the words Batted, never

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cricketer never batted, which upset a rival over their feud.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'about rivalry' is wrong: 'about' signals the letters sit inside 'Batted, never', so the definition is 'rivalry'. 'getting upset' reads them upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter feud between families or rivals is a long-running rivalry.

clue.text: Compass location of container with salt heading east

indicators.note: heading says the salt formula moves on towards the east letter that follows it

parts.note: a bin is a container
NaCl is the chemical formula for common salt

explanation.surface: A ship's container of salt heads east, steered by the compass.
explanation.walkthrough: NaCl is the chemical formula for table salt.
explanation.definitionFit: The housing that holds a ship's compass near the helm is where the compass is located.

clue.text: Snob tipping hat first

indicators.note: tipping means the word for hat is tipped over and read backwards

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
first is written 1st, with 1 as the letter I

explanation.surface: A snob insists on tipping their hat before anyone else does.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE is dated British slang for a hat; 'tipping' turns it to ELIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob looks down on others, as someone believing in rule by a superior few does.

clue.text: Record hit, essence of Queen

parts.note: to tap is to hit lightly

indicators.note: essence of means the central letter of the word Queen

explanation.surface: A hit record capturing the essence of the band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' and 'hit' suggest a pop single; 'essence of' takes the middle E of 'Queen'.
explanation.definitionFit: To record sound or video onto magnetic strip, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Pop, therefore pop?

parts.note: so means therefore
pop and da are both informal words for father

explanation.surface: A child asks whether pop really is just pop.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Pop' is the fizzy drink; the second is dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy drink is called pop, and soda water is a carbonated drink.

clue.text: Suspect's escape curtailed in secure surroundings

indicators.note: in says the shortened escape word goes inside the word for secure

parts.note: sure means secure or safe

indicators.note: curtailed means the last letter of the word for escape is cut off

parts.note: to miss something is to escape it

explanation.surface: A suspect's escape is cut short inside secure surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surroundings' backs up 'in', saying the word for secure goes round the shortened escape word.
explanation.definitionFit: To surmise is to guess without proof, which is to suspect, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Chicken possibly raised as layer

indicators.note: raised means the word for chicken is read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: a chicken is an example of an animal, hence possibly

explanation.surface: A chicken raised to be a laying hen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer' looks like a hen; it means a thin sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin plate or sheet, as in biology or geology, is a layer.

clue.text: Calm extremes of savage rage and noise

indicators.note: extremes of means the first and last letters of each of savage, rage and noise

explanation.surface: Calm prevails at the far ends of savage rage and noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of' takes SE, RE and NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Peaceful and untroubled is a synonym for calm.

clue.text: Direct back over posh beach

indicators.note: over says the reversed word lies across the posh letter, enclosing it
back means the word for direct is read in reverse

parts.note: to direct someone somewhere is to send them
U means upper-class, so posh

explanation.surface: A taxi passenger asks to be directed back over to the posh beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SEND to DNES, which goes 'over' U, the upper-class letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sand hills along the seashore make up a beach, so these mounds stand for the shore.

clue.text: Keeper for a team trapping pass through hole

indicators.note: trapping means the letters are held within the run of words Keeper for a team

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper traps a pass that comes through a hole in the defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapping' signals the answer is held inside 'Keeper for a team'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce something, making a hole that passes right through it, is the verb's meaning.

clue.text: Overweight live in very big house finally

indicators.note: in says the word for live goes inside the letters for very big

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size meaning very big
to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word house

explanation.surface: An overweight person lives in a very big house at last.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a British clothing label for very large garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Very fat, well over a healthy weight, is overweight.

clue.text: Heart is heavier missing husband

indicators.note: missing means the husband letter is dropped from the word for heavier

parts.note: thicker means heavier or more dense

explanation.surface: A doctor notes a widow's heart is heavier with her husband missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes H (husband) from THICKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticker is informal slang for the heart, which ticks like a clock.

clue.text: Home provided in retirement lodge

indicators.note: in retirement means the word for provided goes backwards, retreating

parts.note: if means provided, as in on condition that
to lodge somewhere is to reside there

explanation.surface: A retiree finds a home provided in a retirement lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' turns IF to FI.
explanation.definitionFit: The hearth stands for home and family life, as in fireside comforts.

clue.text: Stops rites regularly following prayer

indicators.note: following says the letters from rites come after the prayer

parts.note: Ave Maria is a prayer, so Ave is a prayer

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word rites is used

explanation.surface: A priest halts the rites at regular intervals after each prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes R, T, S from 'rites'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ward off or prevent something happening is to stop it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Party reversed decline in influence

indicators.note: reversed means the word for party is read backwards

parts.note: a revel is a lively party
to age is to decline with the years

explanation.surface: A political party's reversals have brought a decline in its influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political; it is a revel, which 'reversed' turns to LEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Power to sway outcomes, like the force a lever gives, is influence.
